medium: Acrylic, natural organic pigments, tactile canvas, paper fiber substrate

medium: Black enamel stripes, pin-striping, shaped metallic aluminum canvas
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Kunstmuseum Basel; MoMA (NY)
note: Declared 'what you see is what you see', creating famous Black Paintings and shaped canvases that launched Minimalism.

medium: Mixed media, marble dust, resin, heavy canvas
provenance: Fundació Antoni Tàpies; Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía (Madrid); Museum of Modern Art (MoMA, NY)
note: Pioneered European Matter Painting, constructing relief surfaces out of marble dust and clay that resemble ancient weathered walls.

medium: Motorized scrap iron machinery, self-destructing kinetics, wheels
provenance: Museum Tinguely (Basel); Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY)
note: Created kinetic machine sculptures that make spontaneous drawings and self-destruct in public performances.

medium: Dyed cloth octagons, wire, bubble wrap, fragile plywood attachments
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; Tate Modern
note: Celebrates radical fragility, making subtle wall interventions using wire, paper scraps, and unstretched dyed textiles.

medium: Oil, wax crayon, graphite, raw canvas gesture
provenance: Menil Collection (Houston); Tate Modern (London); Museum of Modern Art (MoMA, NY)
note: Fused classical mythology with energetic scribbles, graffiti-like script, and raw poetic mark-making across off-white canvases.

medium: Hand-hammered nails driven into canvas-covered wooden panels
provenance: Group ZERO Archive; Hamburger Bahnhof (Berlin); Centre Pompidou
note: Group ZERO titan who hammers thousands of industrial nails into canvas fields, creating optical fields of light and shadow.

medium: Oil and acrylic on canvas, geometric optical distortion grids
provenance: Vasarely Museum (Budapest); Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY)
note: Father of Op Art, constructing rigorous geometric grid systems that warp optically to create spatial illusions.

medium: Oil, charcoal, sand on double-sided wooden panels (Dischi series)
provenance: Fondazione Emilio e Annabianca Vedova (Venice); MAXXI (Rome); MoMA (NY)
note: Italian Informel master who painted dramatic black-and-white gestural panels that hang directly in gallery space.

medium: Silkscreen ink and synthetic polymer paint on canvas, serial grids
provenance: Andy Warhol Museum (Pittsburgh); Tate Modern (London); MoMA (NY)
note: Pop Art icon who used mechanical silkscreen repetition to catalog mass culture, celebrity, and consumer identity.

medium: Direct wall typography, language statements, spatial specifications
provenance: Stedelijk Museum (Amsterdam); Whitney Museum (NY); Tate Modern
note: Conceptual legend whose work consisted of written linguistic statements painted directly onto architectural walls.

medium: Resin, plaster, rubber castings of negative spatial voids inside architecture
provenance: Tate Britain (London); National Gallery of Art (DC); Centre Pompidou
note: Renders unseen spatial memory tangible by casting the empty air inside rooms, beds, and architectural structures.

medium: Alkyd and spray paint on aluminum, stenciled block typography, spray erasures
provenance: Guggenheim Museum (NY); Broad Museum (LA); Tate Modern (London)
note: Uses stenciled block lettering and solvent spray erasures to investigate urban linguistic breakdown.

medium: Woven sisal, burlap, resin, bronze headless figure arrays
provenance: National Museum in Wrocław; Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY)
note: Pioneered monumental textile sculpture ('Abakans') and headless crowd forms exploring collective human anonymity.

medium: Paint on transparent Sicofoil sheets, calligraphic sign arrays
provenance: Rivoli Castle Contemporary Art Museum; MAXXI (Rome); Guggenheim Museum (NY)
note: Forma 1 co-founder who painted calligraphic signs on clear plastic Sicofoil to let ambient light act as canvas.

medium: Oil on canvas, atmospheric lyrical color fields, veiled gestural geometries
provenance: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (Rome); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Leading Italian Informel master known for luminous, veiled color planes and poetic architectural geometry.

medium: Folded aluminum reliefs, lenticular optical pigment compositions
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Guggenheim Museum (NY); Tel Aviv Museum of Art
note: Pioneer of Kinetic and Op Art whose lenticular relief surfaces transform visually as the viewer shifts position.

medium: Acrylic on canvas, warped geometric grid compositions, optical ribbon weaves
provenance: Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo; MACBA (Barcelona); Private Archival Collections
note: Constructs intricate, warped geometric grids that explore optical tension and Brazilian modernist textiles.

medium: Acrylic on Masonite, high-contrast complementary color line grids
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Art Institute of Chicago; MoMA (NY)
note: Op Art master who investigated intense color interaction through hyper-precise geometric line repetitions.

medium: Oil on canvas, heavy expressive impasto, primary biomorphic figures
provenance: Rijksmuseum; Stedelijk Museum (Amsterdam); Tate Modern (London)
note: Co-founder of CoBrA who applied thick, tube-squeezed paint to express primal human vitality.

medium: Oil and acrylic on canvas, thin black and color border bands around white voids
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Tate Modern (London); Stedelijk Museum
note: Minimalist painter known for immaculate white square canvases bounded by precise colored edge-bands.

medium: Oil on canvas, speed lines, light decomposition velocity grids
provenance: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (Rome); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern
note: Futurist master whose dynamic velocity lines laid early foundations for post-war mechanical abstraction.

medium: Baked enamel, silkscreen grid lines on steel square plates
provenance: Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Constructed massive, modular grid installations made of hundreds of individual enameled steel square tiles.

medium: Direct architectural wall typography, pigment, site-specific nomenclature grids
provenance: Guggenheim Museum (NY); Museum Ludwig (Cologne); MACBA (Barcelona)
note: Site-specific conceptualist who painted indigenous site names onto museum architecture to critique colonial mapping.

medium: Clay, canvas, natural materials, performance artifact records
provenance: National Gallery of Canada; Art Gallery of Ontario; Documenta Archives
note: First Nations artist who uses performance and raw natural materials to confront Indigenous displacement and memory.

medium: Acrylic on canvas/wood, handwritten white cursive truth aphorisms
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY); MAMAC (Nice)
note: Fluxus titan famous for painting direct, handwritten white philosophical statements across black grounds.

medium: Poured colorful latex, polyurethane foam, pleated bronze paper reliefs
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Pioneered poured latex floor sculptures and pleated metallic knots that challenge rigid Minimalist forms.

medium: Oil and re-applied wash on linen, delicate architectural square geometries
provenance: Kunstmuseum Basel; MoMA (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: Created quiet, luminous abstract squares built from thinned, translucent paint layers.

medium: Motorized chrome, plexiglass light distortion boxes
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires; Houston Museum of Fine Arts
note: Pioneer of Kinetic Art who created motorized, light-refracting kinetic sculptures in 1960s Paris.

medium: Photographic prints mounted with precise semiotic narrative wall texts
provenance: Tate Britain (London); MoMA (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: Conceptual theorist who paired black-and-white photography with rigorous semiotic text panels.

medium: Motorized wooden reliefs, slow-moving nylon/steel wire projections
provenance: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium; Centre Pompidou; Guggenheim Museum (NY)
note: Created motorized kinetic reliefs whose imperceptibly slow movements disrupt traditional sculptural stillness.

medium: Chance-determined I Ching watercolor scores, smoked paper drawings
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: Composer and visual artist who used chance operations and silent duration scores to redefine artistic composition.

medium: Painted white wooden cylinder reliefs, Carrara marble constructions
provenance: Tate Modern (London); MAM Rio; Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: Constructed relief surfaces out of hundreds of angled, white-painted wooden cylinders that catch light.

medium: Compressed crushed automobiles (Compressions), expanded polyurethane foam
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern (London); MoMA (NY)
note: Nouveau Réalisme pioneer known for hydraulically compressed automobile sculptures and expanded foam pours.

medium: Hinged aluminum geometric plates (Bichos), tactile sensory objects
provenance: MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London); Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo
note: Neo-Concrete pioneer whose foldable aluminum geometric sculptures invited physical spectator participation.

medium: Acrylic on canvas, hard-edge perspective highway landscapes, road barrier signs
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); Hirschhorn Museum (DC)
note: Precisionist-Pop painter who reduced American highway infrastructure into stark geometric perspective lines.

medium: Oil and fresco on canvas/wall structures, lyrical poetic color fields
provenance: Stedelijk Museum; Castello di Rivoli; Kunsthalle Basel
note: Transavantgarde member who painted immersive, lyrical color frescoes across entire room walls.

medium: Industrial lacquer on shaped steel plates, hard-edge chromatic architecture
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Carnegie Museum of Art; MoMA (NY)
note: Pioneered industrial lacquer painting on massive steel sheets, creating hard-edge machine abstraction.

medium: Steel I-beams, industrial cranes, unrefined iron timber beams
provenance: Storm King Art Center (NY); Hirschhorn Museum (DC); Louvre Museum
note: Constructs monumental, architectural steel I-beam sculptures that dynamic space.

medium: Artificially rusted iron, charred wood, cotton, cast paper grid wall monuments
provenance: Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY); Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum; Hirschhorn
note: Constructs massive wall reliefs out of artificially weathered and oxidized materials without paint.

medium: Enamel, ink, collaged comic scripts, political text grids on paper/canvas
provenance: GNAM (Rome); MAXXI (Rome); Private European Collections
note: Blends pop-counterculture graphics, political slogans, and natural science diagrams into dense grids.

medium: Handmade neon text, stitched applique fabric blankets, raw gouache/canvas
provenance: Tate Britain (London); Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art; Broad Museum
note: YBA master who translates intimate emotional confession and memory into neon handwriting and stitched textiles.

medium: Alkyd, oil on canvas, dense comic montage narratives, geopolitical collages
provenance: Reykjavík Art Museum; Centre Pompidou (Paris); MACBA (Barcelona)
note: Narrative Figuration titan who paints dense, overwhelming visual montages analyzing mass media propaganda.

medium: Welded copper wire, fused glass lumps, interlocking web structures
provenance: Peggy Guggenheim Collection (Venice); Rodin Museum (Paris); LACMA
note: Pioneered endless, web-like welded copper wire structures enclosing fused glass lumps.

medium: Oil on canvas, vibrant keyhole color shapes, Zen-inspired chromatic fields
provenance: Guggenheim Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); Corcoran Gallery of Art
note: Abstract Expressionist and Color Field precursor known for luminous central keyhole geometry.

medium: Oil, beeswax on canvas, heavy troweled grid gestures, dense mark-making
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Art Institute of Chicago; Jewish Museum (NY)
note: Infused gestural Abstract Expressionism with feminist history, using trowels to build athletic paint grids.

medium: Oil, collage, canvas attachments, sun-disc and boat-hull geometries
provenance: Tate Britain (London); British Council Collection; Leeds Art Gallery
note: St Ives pioneer who abstracted Mediterranean and Cornish light into rhythmic, vibrant semi-circular discs.

medium: Direct wall-painted walk duration typography, framed text records
provenance: Tate Modern (London); MoMA (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: 'Walking Artist' who translates solitary wilderness walks into austere, large-scale wall typography.

medium: Industrial resin, oil, pitch, chemical paint rolls (Industrial Painting)
provenance: Stedelijk Museum; Centre Pompidou; Rivoli Castle
note: Situationist International figure who invented 'Industrial Painting' on long bolts of canvas to critique commodity art.

medium: Nitrocellulose paint on aluminum, modular permutation color panels
provenance: Kunstmuseum Basel; MoMA (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: Swiss graphic design and Op Art master who built mathematical permutation systems out of interchangeable colored aluminum panels.

medium: Color photographic prints, conceptual architectural catalog grids
provenance: MAXXI (Rome); Stedelijk Museum; MoMA (NY)
note: Italian photographer whose quiet catalog grids re-framed landscape and architectural signs as conceptual language.

medium: Hand-tinted framed grid photo-monuments, graphic black window lines
provenance: Tate Modern (London); Stedelijk Museum; MoMA (NY)
note: Living Sculptures who present massive stained-glass-like photo grids documenting urban life, sexuality, and identity.

medium: Erased book pages, paper pulp ribbons, photographic duration logs
provenance: Tate Modern (London); Art Gallery of New South Wales; Guggenheim (NY)
note: Tears and erases historical texts to re-frame colonial language, geography, and material memory.

medium: Oil on canvas, systematic white and grey brush-track modulations
provenance: Sprengel Museum (Hannover); Museum Ludwig (Cologne); Städel Museum
note: German master who devoted his life to analyzing white pigment through rhythmic, horizontal brush-track vibrations.

medium: Oil and acrylic on canvas, floating geometric triangle clusters
provenance: Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY); MoMA (NY); Whitney Museum
note: Abstract Expressionist and Color Field artist known for floating clusters of small, colorful geometric triangular shapes.

medium: Two-way mirror glass pavilions, conceptual magazine text pieces
provenance: Dia Beacon (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern (London)
note: Conceptual legend who constructed two-way mirror glass pavilions that blend spectator reflections with architectural context.

medium: Creosote-soaked timber, fiberglass, steel, industrial structural beams
provenance: Dia Beacon (NY); Walker Art Center; Whitney Museum (NY)
note: Minimalist sculptor who creates massive, low-slung creosote timber and steel structures that alter room scale.

medium: Real-time condensation cubes, institutional visitor poll matrices, text documentation
provenance: Tate Modern (London); Centre Pompidou (Paris); Documenta Archives
note: Pioneered Institutional Critique, documenting socio-political and economic systems governing art museums.

medium: Folded and crumpled canvas (Pliage), oil pigment applied to exposed peaks
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris; Vatican Museums
note: Invented 'Pliage' (folding canvas before painting it), leaving unpainted silent voids when unfolded.

medium: Oil and acrylic on canvas, cheerful wavy grids, glossy paint drips
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Hamburger Bahnhof (Berlin); New Museum (NY)
note: Infused rigid Minimalist geometry with relaxed West Coast pop humor, bright glossy colors, and liquid drips.

medium: Oil on canvas, plastic alphabet geometry (Plastic Alphabet code)
provenance: Musée Matisse; Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern (London)
note: Created 'Plastic Alphabet', a system matching geometric shapes and colors directly to specific letter sounds.

medium: Oil, crayon, ink on canvas, downward bodily perspective, language motifs
provenance: LACMA (Los Angeles); Tate Modern (London); Tamayo Museum (Mexico City)
note: Painted intimate surrealist self-portraits looking down at her own body, integrating environmental language motifs.

medium: Oil on canvas, stenciled commercial numbers and bold word sign matrices
provenance: MoMA (NY); Whitney Museum (NY); Hirschhorn Museum (DC)
note: Pop pioneer who transformed commercial stenciled highway signs, numbers, and words into monumental emblems.

medium: Fluorescent light tubes, scrim translucent fabric, parabolic convex discs
provenance: Dia Beacon (NY); Getty Center (LA); SFMOMA
note: Light and Space titan who used translucent scrim, light, and architectural space to condition pure perception.

medium: Lightboxes, mirrors, photographic records, political text matrices
provenance: Moderna Museet (Stockholm); MAXXI (Rome); Hirschhorn Museum
note: Confronts global humanitarian crises, state violence, and media ethics through lightboxes and mirrors.

medium: Black welded scrap iron, open linear steel space-drawings
provenance: National Gallery of Denmark; Centre Pompidou (Paris); Carnegie Museum
note: Danish master who welded heavy black scrap iron into graceful, weightless spatial drawings.

medium: Thick impasto oil on canvas, Mayan calendar grids, numerical diagrams
provenance: Guggenheim Museum (NY); Hirschhorn Museum; MoMA (NY)
note: Constructed thick, checkerboard-like impasto grids mapping ancient Mayan calendars, math, and physics.

medium: Cut steel plates, heavy iron face cutouts, glass-and-stone balance installations
provenance: Jewish Museum Berlin; Israel Museum; Tate Modern (London)
note: Israeli master famous for 'Fallen Leaves' (thousands of screaming cut-steel iron faces covering gallery floors).

medium: Typewriter ink ribbon drawings on paper, red/black character grid patterns
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago; Museum Ludwig
note: Creates hypnotic visual poetry and pattern grids using manual typewriter ribbon repetitions.

medium: Oil on canvas, 'Body Awareness' expressive figuration
provenance: Albertina (Vienna); MoMA (NY); Stedelijk Museum
note: Pioneered 'Body Awareness' painting, depicting physical sensations and internal bodily feelings from within.

medium: Oil on canvas, dense tactile impasto, wild organic animal motifs
provenance: Museo Ligabue (Gualtieri); Galleria Nazionale Parma
note: Outsider Art titan whose thick, raw paint impasto rendered ferocious wilderness struggles.

medium: Oil on canvas, modular color grids, mathematical structural series
provenance: Kunsthaus Zurich; MoMA (NY); Centre Pompidou (Paris)
note: Concrete Art master who created strict mathematical color modules and non-hierarchical color grids.

medium: Rotor kinetic mirrors, embossed aluminum light reliefs, desert light pillars
provenance: Group ZERO Archive; Museum Ludwig (Cologne); Centre Pompidou
note: Group ZERO co-founder who used polished aluminum, glass, and mirrors to capture natural light reflections.

medium: Kaolin clay on pleated canvas (Achromes), glass wool, bread rolls, cotton
provenance: Fondazione Piero Manzoni; Tate Modern; MoMA (NY)
note: Radical avant-gardist who eliminated color through 'Achromes' (raw canvas soaked in liquid white kaolin clay).

medium: Carved architectural building cuts, photo-documentation, floor section slabs
provenance: Guggenheim Museum (NY); MCA Chicago; Centre Pompidou
note: Pioneered 'Anarchitecture', carving massive geometric slices directly out of abandoned real estate buildings.

medium: Ink and pencil on paper, delicate architectural line grids, diagonal precision
provenance: Tate Modern (London); Met Breuer (NY); Kiran Nadar Museum (New Delhi)
note: Indian minimalist master who created delicate, austere graphite grids exploring architectural space.

medium: Neon tubing at geometric tilt angles, systematic tape grids on canvas
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern (London); MoMA (NY)
note: Co-founder of GRAV who applied mathematical systems and phone-book chance numbers to neon and canvas grids.

medium: Oil on canvas, black ring on white ground, massive monochrome fields
provenance: BMPT Archive; Kunstmuseum Basel; MoMA (NY)
note: BMPT co-founder who repainted the exact same black circle on white canvas over 200 times to neutralize authorship.

medium: Oil, acrylic, torn paper collage on canvas, massive black oval compression gestures
provenance: National Gallery of Art (DC); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern
note: Intellectual leader of Abstract Expressionism famous for 'Elegies to the Spanish Republic' (black ovals compressed between vertical bars).

medium: Useless Machines (Macchine Inutili), polarized light slides, paper geometric folds
provenance: Museo del Novecento (Milan); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern
note: Futurist and kinetic pioneer who created light-weight 'Useless Machines' suspended in space to catch air currents.

medium: Oil on canvas, pale rocky earth tones, haunting Dachau survivor figures
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Museo Reina Sofía; Venice Biennale Archives
note: Concentration camp survivor who painted muted, stone-colored landscapes and haunting, tragic human bodies.

medium: Stretched pantyhose, sand, performance duration, foam attachments
provenance: MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London); Studio Museum in Harlem
note: Pioneered 'RŠS33' sculptures using sand-filled nylon pantyhose stretched under tension across gallery corners.

medium: Carved basalt, granite, Akari paper lanterns, interlocking marble slabs
provenance: Noguchi Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Merged Japanese traditional stone carving with Western modernism, treating raw basalt and space as unified environment.

medium: Wearable capes (Parangolés), colored sand, labyrinth architectural rooms
provenance: Tate Modern (London); MAM Rio; MoMA (NY)
note: Neo-Concrete leader who invented 'Parangolés' (wearable fabric capes activated through dance) and Tropicalia environments.

medium: Soft vinyl, canvas stuffed with kapok, giant steel monument sculptures
provenance: MoMA (NY); Whitney Museum (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Pop pioneer who transformed rigid household objects and food items into giant, drooping soft vinyl sculptures.

medium: Paraloid paint on canvas, line-circle-dot primordial gestures
provenance: Tate Britain (London); SFMOMA; Oakland Museum of California
note: Surrealist and Dynaton co-founder who pared painting down to primordial 'line, circle, dot' calligraphic marks.

medium: Poetic flying machines, balsa wood, leather, bicycle chains, motors
provenance: S.M.A.K. (Ghent); Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium; Centre Pompidou
note: Belgian visionary who constructed poetic, non-functional flying machines and submarines bridging art and physics.

medium: Hand-drawn pencil lines in wet white oil paint (Écriture), layered Hanji paper
provenance: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Korea); Guggenheim (NY); M+
note: Father of Dansaekhwa (Korean Monochrome) famous for repetitive pencil carvings made into wet paint and Hanji paper.

medium: Perspex, gravure, wood reliefs, linear spiral abstractions
provenance: Tate Britain (London); British Council Collection; Yale Center for British Art
note: Pioneered British abstract relief construction, using perspex and wooden shapes to structure environmental space.

medium: Blown glass, horsehair, parchment, organic anatomical casings
provenance: Guggenheim Bilbao; Centre Pompidou (Paris); Museo Reina Sofía
note: Constructs fragile, unsettling sculptural casings using blown glass, intestines, and organic hair.

medium: Sponge, pumice stone, industrial zinc, oil on panel (Polymaterial art)
provenance: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (Rome); Centre Pompidou; MART Trento
note: Futurist pioneer of 'Polymaterialism', constructing reliefs out of pumice stone, sponge, and sheet metal.

medium: Oil on canvas, commercial brand icon matrices, pin-up consumer juxtapositions
provenance: Whitney Museum (NY); MoMA (NY); Museum Ludwig (Cologne)
note: Pop painter who satirized mass-media advertising by pairing commercial consumer products with magazine imagery.

medium: Oil on canvas, ultra-matte oil-drained black cruciform grids (Black Paintings)
provenance: MoMA (NY); Guggenheim Museum (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Created famous 'Black Paintings'—matte black square canvases featuring barely visible cruciform grids.

medium: Heavy knife-applied paint impasto, mosaic-like paint squeeze strata
provenance: National Gallery of Canada; Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern
note: Les Automatistes master who applied pure paint directly from tubes using palette knives to create mosaic-like crusts.

medium: Oil, charcoal, photo collage on canvas, smudged history narratives
provenance: MoMA (NY); Whitney Museum (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Bridged Abstract Expressionism and Pop Art by combining smudged charcoal marks with historical commercial icons.

medium: Torn street movie posters mounted on canvas (Décollage)
provenance: MAXXI (Rome); Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY)
note: Nouveau Réalisme pioneer who invented 'Décollage', ripping down layers of street movie posters to reveal urban history.

medium: Papier-mâché, white latex paint on cardboard grid wall reliefs
provenance: NUL Group Archive; Stedelijk Museum; Tate Modern (London)
note: NUL Group co-founder who built immaculate white geometric grid reliefs out of cardboard and papier-mâché.

medium: Thin steel rods suspended in front of striped wood panels, nylon threads (Penetrables)
provenance: Centre Pompidou (Paris); Tate Modern (London); MoMA (NY)
note: Kinetic master who created 'Penetrables' (walk-through rooms made of thousands of hanging yellow nylon cords).

medium: Electromagnets, floating steel needles, radio antenna signals (Signals)
provenance: Tate Modern (London); Centre Pompidou (Paris); MoMA (NY)
note: Pioneered Kinetic Sculptures using invisible electromagnetic fields to suspend heavy steel needles in mid-air.

medium: Temperament wash, white calligraphic brushwork webs (White Writing)
provenance: Seattle Art Museum; MoMA (NY); Tate Modern (London)
note: Pioneered 'White Writing' (dense, web-like white calligraphic brushwork inspired by Chinese calligraphy).

medium: Cast bronze, raw wood, acrylic on canvas, totem-like vertical forms
provenance: Tate Britain (London); Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art; Hirschhorn
note: British sculptor and painter who built minimalist bronze totem poles and flat Color Field canvases.

medium: Dye on unstretched, unhemmed military tarp/fabric (Supports/Surfaces)
provenance: Supports/Surfaces Archive; Centre Pompidou; MoMA (NY)
note: Supports/Surfaces co-founder who repeatedly stamped a single sponge-like shape onto unstretched hanging tarps.
